message.content:
I don’t have direct access to your **VirusTotal** account (or any other external service), so I can’t pull live data for you.  
What I *can* give you is a quick recipe you can copy‑paste into your own script or Postman collection to hit the endpoint yourself:

---

### 1️⃣ Build the Request  

| Element | Value |
|---------|-------|
| Base URL | `https://www.virustotal.com` |
| Endpoint | `/api/v3/ip_addresses/{ip}/files` – replace `{ip}` with `178.34.55.101` |
| Query Params | `limit=15`, `cursor=next_set` |
| Method | `GET` |

Full URL example:
```
https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/178.34.55.101/files?limit=15&cursor=next_set
```

> ⚠️ If you’re already paginating through results, make sure you pass the exact value returned in the previous page’s `"links.next"` field instead of literally “next_set”.

---

### 2️⃣ Set Up Authentication  

Add an HTTP header:

```http
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_SUPER_API_KEY_HERE
```

Replace `YOUR_SUPER_API_KEY_HERE` with the **Super API Key** you received when creating your VT account. Keep this token secret—don’t commit it to public repos!

---

### 3️⃣ Send & Parse the Response  

A successful call returns something like:

```json
{
    "data": [
        {
            "id": "abcd1234efgh5678",
            "attributes": { ... },
            ...
        },
        …
    ],
    "meta": { … }
}
```

To extract just the **file ID** (`data[*].id`) and its **context attributes**, you’d iterate over each item in the `data` array and pick out those two fields.

#### Example in Python (requests)

```python
import requests

url = ("https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/"
       f"ip_addresses/178.34.55.101/files"
       "?limit=15&cursor=next_set")

headers = {"x-apikey": "<SUPER_API_KEY>"}

resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers)
if resp.status_code == 200:
    json_resp = resp.json()
    for entry in json_resp["data"]:
        print("ID:", entry["id"])
        # Context attributes may appear under various nested keys;
        # adjust based on what you see in the raw payload.
else:
    print(f"Error {resp.status_code}: {resp.text}")
```

*(If you prefer cURL)*

```bash
curl -H "x-apikey: <SUPER_API_KEY>" \
     "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/178.34.55.101/files?limit=15&cursor=next_set"
```

---

### 4️⃣ Pagination Tips  

- Each response contains a `"links"` object. Use `"links.next"` for the next page’s cursor value.
- Rate limiting applies: free accounts usually allow ~4 k queries/day, paid tiers higher. Check the docs for precise numbers.

---

### 5️⃣ What You’ll Get  

With the above call you’ll receive up to 15 file objects per page. For each one you can read:

- `id`: the unique identifier used across VT endpoints.
- Any contextual metadata exposed in the same record (e.g., first seen time, last seen time, tags).  
  These often sit inside sub‑objects like `last_analysis_stats`, `first_submission_date`, etc.—so inspect the full JSON structure to locate exactly where “context” lives for your needs.

---

That’s basically everything you need to run the query locally. Once you’ve got the raw JSON back, feel free to share anonymized snippets here if you’d like help filtering or interpreting specific parts!
